## Tableau Authentication Setup

### For Tableau Cloud:
- **Server URL**: Use your Tableau Cloud URL (e.g., https://10az.online.tableau.com or https://us-east-1.online.tableau.com)
- **Site Content URL**: Your site name (leave empty for default site)

### For Tableau Server:
- **Server URL**: Your Tableau Server URL (e.g., https://tableau.yourcompany.com)
- **Site Content URL**: Your site name (leave empty for default site)

### Authentication Methods:
Choose **either** Username/Password **or** Personal Access Token:

#### Option 1: Username and Password
- Enter your Tableau username and password
- For Tableau Cloud, use your email address as username
- For Tableau Server, use your domain\username if using Active Directory

#### Option 2: Personal Access Token (Recommended)
- Go to your Tableau account settings
- Generate a Personal Access Token
- Enter the token name and secret

**Security Note:** Personal Access Tokens are recommended for production use as they provide better security and can be revoked individually.

aiMetadata.description: Queues an immediate extract refresh for a workbook (by workbook ID), starting a background job on the Tableau site and returning its job identifier. Use to update a workbook's extracted data on demand. Not idempotent: each call enqueues a new refresh job.

find_view.name: find_view
find_view.description: Finds a view based on name (URL name)

viewName.description: The URL name of the view to find (e.g., Sheet1 from /views/workbook/Sheet1)

aiMetadata.description: Looks up a single Tableau view by its URL name (the slug from /views/workbook/<name>, e.g. "Sheet1") and returns its metadata including the resolved view ID, owner, workbook, and project. Use to resolve a human-facing view name into the ID needed by other actions; errors if no matching view exists. Read-only and idempotent.

find_workbook.name: find_workbook
find_workbook.description: Finds a workbook based on ID or content URL

searchType.description: Choose whether to search by workbook ID or content URL

workbookId.description: The ID of the workbook to find

contentUrl.description: The content URL of the workbook to find (e.g., "MyWorkbook" from /workbooks/MyWorkbook)

aiMetadata.description: Looks up a single Tableau workbook and returns its full metadata (name, project, owner, views, timestamps). Search By selects the lookup mode: by workbook ID, or by content URL (the slug from /workbooks/<name>) — supply the field matching the chosen mode. Use to resolve a workbook reference into details or its ID; errors if not found. Read-only and idempotent.

workbook_event.name: workbook_event
workbook_event.description: Triggers when a workbook event occurs (created, updated, or deleted)

eventType.description: Select the workbook event to trigger on

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a workbook lifecycle event happens on the Tableau site — one of created, updated, or deleted, selected via the Event Type. Represents a single workbook change and carries the affected workbook's name and ID.

workbook_refresh_event.name: workbook_refresh_event
workbook_refresh_event.description: Triggers when a workbook refresh event occurs (started, succeeded, or failed)

eventType.description: Select the workbook refresh event to trigger on

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a workbook extract refresh reaches a chosen stage on the Tableau site — refresh started, succeeded, or failed, selected via the Event Type. Use to react to the progress or outcome of a workbook refresh; the payload identifies the affected workbook.

datasource_event.name: datasource_event
datasource_event.description: Triggers when a datasource event occurs (created, updated, or deleted)

eventType.description: Select the datasource event to trigger on

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a datasource lifecycle event happens on the Tableau site — one of created, updated, or deleted, selected via the Event Type. Represents a single datasource change and carries the affected datasource's name and ID.

datasource_refresh_event.name: datasource_refresh_event
datasource_refresh_event.description: Triggers when a datasource refresh event occurs (started, succeeded, or failed)

eventType.description: Select the datasource refresh event to trigger on

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a datasource extract refresh reaches a chosen stage on the Tableau site — refresh started, succeeded, or failed, selected via the Event Type. Use to react to the progress or outcome of a datasource refresh; the payload identifies the affected datasource.

user_deleted.name: user_deleted
user_deleted.description: Triggers when a user is deleted

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a user is removed from the Tableau site. Represents a single user-deletion event and carries the deleted user's name and ID.

view_deleted.name: view_deleted
view_deleted.description: Triggers when a workbook view is deleted

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a view within a workbook is deleted on the Tableau site. Represents a single view-deletion event and carries the deleted view's name and ID.

label_event.name: label_event
label_event.description: Triggers when a label event occurs (created, updated, or deleted)

eventType.description: Select the label event to trigger on

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a label (e.g. a data-quality or sensitivity label on a content asset) changes on the Tableau site — one of created, updated, or deleted, selected via the Event Type. Carries the affected asset's name and ID.

new_job.name: new_job
new_job.description: Triggers when a job matches the specified criteria

aiMetadata.description: Polls the Tableau site's background jobs and fires for each newly created job, optionally narrowed by Job Type (e.g. refresh extracts, run flow) and Status (e.g. Success, Failed, InProgress); leaving a filter empty matches all values for it. Use to watch for new or completed background jobs.

list_extract_refresh_tasks.name: list_extract_refresh_tasks
list_extract_refresh_tasks.description: Lists extract refresh tasks for the site

aiMetadata.description: Polls the configured extract refresh tasks on the Tableau site and fires for each newly seen task, surfacing its schedule and the workbook or datasource it targets. Use to detect when a new extract refresh task is added to the site.

## Tableau Authentifizierung Setup

### Für Tableau Cloud:
- **Server URL**: Verwenden Sie Ihre Tableau Cloud URL (z.B. https://10az.online.tableau.com oder https://us-east-1.online.tableau. om)
- **Site Content URL**: Your site name (leave leer für die Standardseite)

### For Tableau Server:
- **Server URL**: Your Tableau Server URL (e. ., https://tableau.yourcompany. om)
- **Site Content URL**: Ihre Site Name (lassen Sie leer für die Standardseite)

### Authentifizierungsmethoden:
Wählen Sie **entweder** Benutzername/Passwort **or** Persönliches Zugangs-Token:

#### Option 1: Benutzername und Passwort
- Geben Sie Ihren Tableau Benutzernamen und Passwort
- Für Tableau Cloud, verwenden Sie Ihre E-Mail-Adresse als Benutzername
- Für Tableau Server, Verwenden Sie Ihre Domain\username wenn Sie Active Directory

#### Option 2: Persönliches Zugangs-Token (Empfohlen)
- Gehen Sie zu Ihren Kontoeinstellungen
- Erstellen Sie ein persönliches Zugangs-Token
- Geben Sie den Token-Namen und das Geheimnis

**Sicherheits-Hinweis:** Persönliche Zugriffs-Token werden für die Produktion empfohlen, da sie für bessere Sicherheit sorgen und individuell widerrufen werden können.

fr.\n## Tableau Authentication Setup\n\n###:
## Configuration d'authentification Tableau

### Pour Tableau Cloud:
- **URL du serveur** : Utilisez l'URL de votre Tableau Cloud (par exemple, https://10az.online.tableau.com ou https://us-east-1.online.tableau. om)
- **URL du contenu** : le nom de votre site (laisser vide pour le site par défaut)

### Pour Tableau Server :
- **URL du serveur** : URL de votre serveur Tableau (e. ., https://tableau.yourcompany. om)
- **URL du contenu du site** : le nom de votre site (laisser vide pour le site par défaut)

### Méthodes d'authentification :
Choisissez **soit** Nom d'utilisateur/mot de passe **ou** Jeton d'accès personnel :

#### Option 1 : Nom d'utilisateur et mot de passe
- Entrez votre nom d'utilisateur Tableau et votre mot de passe
- Pour Tableau Cloud, utiliser votre adresse e-mail comme nom d'utilisateur
- Pour le serveur Tableau, Utilisez votre domaine\nom d'utilisateur si vous utilisez Active Directory

#### Option 2: Jeton d'accès personnel (Recommandé)
- Allez dans les paramètres de votre compte Tableau
- Générez un jeton d'accès personnel
- Entrez le nom du jeton et le secret

**Note de sécurité :** Les jetons d'accès personnels sont recommandés pour une utilisation de production car ils fournissent une meilleure sécurité et peuvent être révoqués individuellement.

## Tableau Authentication Setup

### For Tableau Cloud:
- **Server URL**: Use your Tableau Cloud URL (e.g., https://10az.online.tableau.com or https://us-east-1.online.tableau.com)
- **Site Content URL**: Your site name (leave empty for default site)

### For Tableau Server:
- **Server URL**: Your Tableau Server URL (e.g., https://tableau.yourcompany.com)
- **Site Content URL**: Your site name (leave empty for default site)

### Authentication Methods:
Choose **either** Username/Password **or** Personal Access Token:

#### Option 1: Username and Password
- Enter your Tableau username and password
- For Tableau Cloud, use your email address as username
- For Tableau Server, use your domain\username if using Active Directory

#### Option 2: Personal Access Token (Recommended)
- Go to your Tableau account settings
- Generate a Personal Access Token
- Enter the token name and secret

**Security Note:** Personal Access Tokens are recommended for production use as they provide better security and can be revoked individually.

pt.\n## Tableau Authentication Setup\n\n###:
## Configuração de autenticação Tableau

### Para Tableau Cloud:
- **URL do servidor**: Use seu URL Tableau Cloud (p. ex., https://10az.online.tableau.com ou https://us-east-1.online.tableau. om)
- **URL do conteúdo do site**: Nome do seu site (deixe em branco para site padrão)

### Para Tableau Server:
- **URL do servidor**: Sua URL do servidor Tableau (e. ., https://tableau.yourempresa. om)
- **URL do conteúdo do site**: Nome do seu site (deixe em branco para site padrão)

### Métodos de autenticação:
Escolha **ou** Nome de usuário/senha **ou** Token de Acesso Pessoal:

#### Opção 1: Nome de usuário e senha
- Digite seu nome de usuário e senha
- Para Tableau Cloud, usar seu endereço de e-mail como nome de usuário
- Para servidor Tableau, Use seu nome-de-domínio\username usando Active Directory

#### Opção 2: Token de Acesso Pessoal (Recomendado)
- Vá para suas configurações de conta Tableau
- Gerar um Token de Acesso Pessoal
- Insira o nome do token e o nome secreto

**Nota de Segurança:** Tokens de Acesso Pessoal são recomendados para uso da produção, pois fornecem melhor segurança e podem ser revogados individualmente.
